expect.note: evals.run.over_budget is the whole ruling: only `fast` carries a ceiling, 60.00s is inside it and 60.01s is not, and evals/run.py applies it to the run it just measured

provenance: the `fast` gate's wall clock went 13s (M2) -> 48.6s (M6) -> 55.4s (M7) -> 67.5s (M8) without one run ever turning red, because ADR-002 Decision 4's 60s ceiling was prose in an ADR and nothing read it. The first version of this case read `sorted(evals/report/*-fast.json)[-1]` and was falsified in review (PR #20 R1): on a fresh clone — which is exactly what `.github/workflows/eval.yml` does — the newest file is always the report the branch committed, so a tree measuring 77.23s still scored 89/89 = 1.000 and the gate stayed green. A guard that cannot see the run it belongs to is the same comment the prose ceiling was. The ruling now lives in `evals.run.over_budget`, is applied to the current run's `totals.wall_seconds`, and exits non-zero; this case grades the ruling. Watched red before the fix existed: `ImportError: cannot import name 'WALL_BUDGET_S' from 'evals.run'`, this case alone, 88/89 = 0.989 against baseline 1.000.

triage.note: two halves that have to stay in sync: `evals/run.py` applies the ceiling to the run it just measured (a report written after the run, and discarded with a CI workspace, can never gate it), and this case pins the ruling — the boundary at 60.00/60.01, and that `fast` is the only suite carrying one, so a later edit cannot quietly widen it or move it onto another suite. Deliberately NOT tagged `invariant`: invariants are absolute and machine-independent, and a wall clock is neither — ADR-009 Decision 6 records the same suite measuring 66.6-68.3s here and 68.6s on a reviewer's machine.
triage.not_covered: it grades total wall clock only — a case that gets 10s slower while another gets 10s faster is invisible to it; per-case timings are in every committed report for anyone looking. It also does not settle what a contributor on slower hardware should do when the ceiling is genuinely unreachable there, which is an open policy question (PR #20 R6, Debt T-R6).
